Visit note | 2025-04-19 11:00 AM | Dr. Tahmina Begum, Dermatology | Patient: Champa Hasan, 38, female. Ms. Hasan reports having itchy raised welts that come and go, along with occasional swelling of her lips. She mentions that these symptoms began after taking a new painkiller bought in Kushtia. She works as a journalist and lives a busy lifestyle. She has no known comorbidities and denies any breathing difficulty or abdominal pain. Examination reveals about 24 welts on the trunk and arms, while other vitals show a blood pressure of 127/84 mmHg, pulse of 68 bpm, and weight of 85 kg. The skin elsewhere is warm and dry. Assessment: Acute urticaria. Plan: a prescription was issued today. She was advised to avoid the suspected food or medication, keep a detailed symptom diary, and go to hospital at once if her tongue or throat swells. Follow-up in 2 weeks with the symptom diary.

Visit note | 2025-04-19 11:00 AM | Dr. Fahmida Yasmin, ENT | Patient: Saiful Khan, 35, male. Mr. Khan presents with painful swallowing, a high fever, and a sore throat that began after an outbreak at a school in Keraniganj. He works as a cricket coach and is active outdoors. He has no chronic medical conditions and denies cough or shortness of breath. On examination, his temperature is 101.0°F, blood pressure is 131/71 mmHg, pulse is 98 bpm, and weight is 63 kg. Throat examination shows red, enlarged tonsils with small exudates. Assessment: Acute tonsillitis. Plan: a prescription was issued for supportive and symptomatic relief. He was advised to gargle with warm salt water, eat soft foods, and drink plenty of fluids. Follow-up in 1 week.

Visit note | 2025-04-19 11:00 AM | Dr. Nazma Begum, Obstetrics and Gynecology | Patient: Lipi Pramanik, 20, female. Ms. Pramanik attends for a review regarding extra hair growth on her face, increasingly irregular periods, and noticeable weight gain, which she first noticed after a friend in Gazipur suggested testing. She works as a bank officer and has a sedentary routine. She has no chronic comorbidities and denies pelvic pain or severe headaches. Examination shows her BMI is 31.3, blood pressure is 113/72 mmHg, pulse is 76 bpm, and weight is 86 kg. Mild facial hirsutism is noted. Assessment: Polycystic ovary syndrome. Plan: a prescription was issued to help regulate cycles. She was advised to aim for a 5% weight loss, exercise for 150 minutes a week, and reduce sugary drinks. Follow-up in 3 months.

Visit note | 2025-04-19 12:00 PM | Dr. Farhana Kabir, General Medicine | Patient: Nusrat Gazi, 46, female. Mrs. Gazi attends for a review, stating she has been looking quite pale and getting breathless when climbing stairs. She noticed these issues after months of skipping lunch during her long driving shifts in Khilgaon. She works as a bus driver and has no other major health problems. She denies chest pain, dizziness, or gastrointestinal bleeding. On examination, her haemoglobin is 8.8 g/dL, blood pressure is 111/85 mmHg, pulse is 70 bpm, and weight is 79 kg. Conjunctivae appear pale. Assessment: Iron deficiency anaemia. Plan: a prescription was issued for iron supplementation. She was advised to eat more lentils, spinach, liver, and eggs, and to avoid drinking tea within an hour of meals. Follow-up in 6 weeks with a repeat haemoglobin test.

Visit note | 2025-04-19 12:00 PM | Dr. Nasrin Sultana, Gastroenterology | Patient: Tushar Bhattacharya, 31, male. Mr. Bhattacharya attends for follow-up, reporting a persistent sour taste in his mouth, symptoms that worsen when lying down, and a burning sensation behind his breastbone after meals. He notes this became worse after weeks of eating fried snacks at tea stalls in Cox's Bazar. He works as a homemaker and denies difficulty swallowing or unexplained weight loss. On examination, his BMI is 26.5, blood pressure is 133/85 mmHg, pulse is 87 bpm, and weight is 64 kg. Abdominal examination is soft with mild epigastric tenderness. Assessment: Gastro-oesophageal reflux disease. Plan: a prescription was issued to manage acid reflux. He was advised to eat smaller meals, avoid oily and spicy food late at night, and raise the head of his bed. Follow-up in 1 month.

Visit note | 2025-04-19 12:00 PM | Dr. Mostafizur Rahman, Orthopedics | Patient: Salma Begum, 62, female. Mrs. Begum attends for a follow-up visit, reporting worsening knee pain when using stairs and a noticeable creaking sound in her knee. She states this has been much worse since moving to a building with no lift in Cox's Bazar. She is a retired civil servant and has a history of Essential hypertension. She denies locking or sudden giving way of the joint. Examination reveals a BMI of 32.4, blood pressure of 148/88 mmHg, pulse of 82 bpm, and weight of 83 kg. Crepitus is palpable in both knees with reduced range of flexion. Assessment: Knee osteoarthritis. Plan: a prescription was issued for pain management. She was advised to do thigh-strengthening exercises daily, lose weight, and avoid squatting or sitting cross-legged on the floor. Follow-up in 6 weeks with physiotherapy.

Visit note | 2025-04-19 12:30 PM | Dr. Rumana Haque, Endocrinology | Patient: Jubayer Munshi, 58, male. Examination reveals a fasting glucose of 11.0 mmol/L, blood pressure of 120/84 mmHg, pulse of 82 bpm, and weight of 85 kg. Systemic examination is otherwise unremarkable. Assessment: Type 2 diabetes mellitus. Plan: a prescription was issued for glucose-lowering therapy. He was advised to reduce rice portions and sweets, walk briskly for 30 minutes five days a week, check his fasting sugar twice weekly, and check his feet daily. Follow-up in 3 months with HbA1c.
